M11 icon pilot — style checkpoint

Sixteen file-type icons generated as one 4×4 sheet by Nano Banana Pro through the agy CLI, then sliced, alpha-keyed and vectorised locally. This page is the style gate: the question is not "are these nice at 64 px" (they are) but "do they hold at 16 px in a real explorer tree".

1 sheet = 16 icons 1024×1024 native 35–42 s per sheet vtracer 0.6.5 ImageMagick 7.1.2

4 — True 16 px pixel grid

Downscaled to a real 16×16 raster, then blown up 8× with nearest-neighbour so the actual delivered pixels are visible. This is the honest view — and where the raster route shows its seams: every glyph is soft and off-grid, because these are downsampled paintings, not pixel-hinted vectors.

5 — Raster vs traced vector

Left of each pair: the keyed PNG. Right: the vtracer SVG after 5-colour posterisation. Trace fidelity is good at display size; the cost is file weight — a hand-authored VS Code file icon is well under 2 KB.

6 — Source sheets

Two independent runs of the identical prompt. Style drift between them is very low — the style block is reproducible, which is the single most important property for growing this to a full set.

7 — Pipeline results

1. Generate
worked		 agy -p … --dangerously-skip-permissions One 4x4 sheet per call, 35 s and 42 s for the two runs. All 16 cells present, in the requested order, on the first try — no retries for content.
2. Resolution
partial		 requested 2048², got 1024² Two runs, both returned 1024². The agent reported 1024² as "native output resolution returned by the model". Cells are therefore 256², not 512².
3. Slice
worked		 magick -crop 4x4@ Grid is geometrically regular; a blind 4x4 division landed every icon inside its cell with margin to spare. Zero manual nudging.
4. Key
worked		 fuzz 14% + 4-corner floodfill Sheet background was a true #FFFFFF. Floodfill (not global -transparent) was required so white letters *inside* badges survive.
5. Flatness
failed		 measured %k unique colours The "flat, no gradients" instruction was not obeyed at pixel level: the TS badge holds 12,255 unique colours, CSS 24,735. Output is quietly photographic.
6. Vectorize
partial		 vtracer 0.6.5, spline Raw trace = 207 paths / 108 KB for one badge. Posterising to 5 colours first drops that to 14 paths / 29 KB — usable, still ~20× a hand-authored icon.

8 — The exact command

--dangerously-skip-permissions was required: without it the run dies in 20 s with "a tool required the "command" permission that headless mode cannot prompt for". --mode accept-edits alone is not enough.

agy -p "$PROMPT" \ --add-dir /Users/sebastian.suarez/Projects/VSebCode/m11-icons/pilot \ --mode accept-edits \ --dangerously-skip-permissions \ --print-timeout 8m

9 — Master prompt, verbatim

Prefixed at call time with: "Using Nano Banana Pro, generate the image described below and save it to <path> at full resolution…"

A single square image: a 4x4 grid of 16 file-type icons for a code editor, evenly spaced cells, generous padding, NO grid lines, on a UNIFORM PURE WHITE background (#FFFFFF everywhere outside the icons).

UNIFORM STYLE — these 16 icons are ONE matched set: flat 2D vector look, solid matte colors, bold simple geometry that stays readable at 16x16 pixels, subtly rounded corners, NO gradients, NO outlines, NO drop shadows, NO 3D, NO texture, NO background tiles behind silhouettes, and NO text anywhere except the short letter badges explicitly specified. Matte desaturated-bright colors tuned for a near-black editor UI (#121314).

Exactly three archetypes: (A) BADGE = rounded square filled with the brand color carrying 1-3 bold white (or specified) letters; (B) SILHOUETTE = one flat object shape in the brand color; (C) GLYPH = a bold flat monogram/mark drawn directly in the brand color with no shape behind it.

Cells left-to-right, top-to-bottom:

6. HTML — SILHOUETTE: flat shield #E44D26 with white number 5
7. Python — GLYPH: the two-snakes interlocked mark, simplified flat, #3776AB and #FFD43B
8. Rust — GLYPH: simplified flat gear with letter R, #DEA584
9. Go — BADGE #00ADD8, white letters GO

16. Plain file — SILHOUETTE: flat document with folded corner, light gray #C5C5C5
